reading.body:
Digital Realty's LAX10 facility in downtown Los Angeles covers 489,500 square feet across 7 stories with N+1 redundancy for power and cooling. The operator has not published a power capacity figure for this campus, so its actual IT load cannot be determined from the specification. The building holds SOC2, SOC3, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001 certifications, which qualify it for workloads requiring security and compliance controls across financial services, healthcare, and general enterprise use cases.

LAX10 sits in California, a state where 11 data center facilities have published power capacity online, totaling 365 MW of reported IT load across 103 mapped locations. Without a published power figure, this facility cannot be ranked against peers within the state. The lack of capacity data means LAX10 does not contribute to the known supply picture for AI infrastructure in California, despite its size and location.

The campus offers access to over 25 network providers and seismic resilience for the Los Angeles region. These attributes would support multi-tenant enterprise and financial workloads. Whether LAX10 hosts meaningful AI training or inference capacity depends on its actual power provisioning and the operator's design choices for IT load, neither of which are published on the facility's specification page.
